dedupe_keys.name: population body mass and food energy requirements for 186 countries 1975 2014

description: This table shows how much food energy the populations of 186 countries needed each year from 1975 to 2014, taking into account that people have become older, taller and heavier. The producers are Felipe Vásquez, Gibran Vita and Daniel B. Müller of the Industrial Ecology Programme at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology, who used it in a 2018 Sustainability article on food security for an ageing and heavier population. Coverage is national and global, with population, average food energy requirement, body weight, height and age for each country and year. It is available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence; the record carries the article's identifier. Caveats: requirements are modelled from demographic and anthropometric averages, not measured intake, the series ends in 2014, and within-country differences are not shown. Simulation uses: converting population projections into food energy demand for national food supply models, and adjusting supply requirements in emergency food planning for older or heavier populations. Related records: FAOSTAT food balances (data-faostat) give the supply side, and the global food security projections database (data-global-food-security-projections-database) gives future demand.
